status_summary: On 2025-10-21 DOE issued a solicitation to buy one million barrels for the reserve, citing $171 million appropriated to begin refilling it and restore it to full operational capacity. On 2026-03-11 DOE announced release of 172 million barrels as its share of a coordinated 400 million-barrel International Energy Agency action, stating the aim of lowering energy prices and citing threats to energy security from Iran and its proxies, with about 200 million barrels to be returned within a year. On 2026-09-29 DOE issued a request for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels under that commitment, describing it as addressing short-term supply disruptions and providing for return of the barrels plus premium barrels to raise long-term inventory. The September notice states that five earlier solicitations had awarded more than 133 million barrels across four completed exchanges, with a 25 percent premium in earlier returns.

timeline.event: DOE issued a solicitation to purchase one million barrels of crude oil for the Bryan Mound site, citing $171 million appropriated to begin refilling the reserve.

DOE announced the release of 172 million barrels from the reserve as the U.S. share of a coordinated 400 million-barrel International Energy Agency action, which DOE says member nations agreed at the President's request to lower energy prices; the statement also cites threats to energy security from Iran and its proxies, states that delivery would take about 120 days, and says about 200 million barrels are to be returned within a year.

DOE issued a request for proposals for an exchange of up to 40 million barrels from the Big Hill and Bryan Mound sites under the 172 million-barrel commitment, citing short-term supply disruptions, with borrowed barrels returned plus premium barrels; bids were due 2026-10-06. The notice states that five earlier solicitations had awarded more than 133 million barrels across four completed exchanges.

title: Keep the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for strategic purposes, not political price ends
uncertainties: Stage reflects a judgment. The Mandate asks that the reserve be maintained for national strategic purposes and not misused for political gain. DOE's March 2026 statement names lowering energy prices as an aim alongside Iran-related energy security threats, while its September 2026 statement describes the releases as an IEA response to short-term supply disruptions structured as exchanges that add premium barrels. A trade report states the reserve fell to its lowest level since 1982 and that returns run to late 2028; this was not reconciled against EIA inventory data. Searches run on energy.gov and trade news. The SPR provisions of P.L. 119-21 could not be read: the GovInfo HTML text returned was cut short in the agriculture title and did not reach the energy sections, and the law.cornell.edu notes for 42 U.S.C. 6240 end in 2013 and do not reflect the law; the DOE solicitation names the appropriation of $171 million but cites no public law number or section. The DOE statement of March 2026 describes lower energy prices as the President's request to partner nations, which bears on the Mandate's point about political price ends; the stage and match remain a judgment.
